thumb-1920-374856.jpg: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima. Joe Rosenthal, Feb. 23, 1945. Six Marines raise the second, larger flag atop Mount Suribachi during the battle for Iwo Jima; one of the most reproduced photographs in history.
H-003-1 Asheville's Defiance.jpg: USS Asheville (PG-21), the first Navy ship named for the city, commissioned in 1920. After years showing the flag from Central America to China, she retreated toward Australia as the Philippines fell, and was sunk south of Java on March 3, 1942, by a Japanese cruiser and two destroyers. Nearly her entire crew was lost.
USS_Asheville_(PG-84)_underway_in_1966.j: USS Asheville (PG-84), an Asheville-class patrol gunboat commissioned in 1966 and deployed to Vietnam's coastal waters under Operation Market Time, intercepting enemy supply traffic; the second Navy ship to carry the city's name.
US_Navy_060215-N-9500T-045_The_Los_Angel: USS Asheville (SSN-758), today's Asheville, a Los Angeles-class fast attack submarine commissioned in 1991. Now homeported in Guam with the U.S. Pacific Fleet, she's the third Navy vessel to carry the city's name.
